items.title: NSE joins Rs 5 lakh crore m-cap club, overtakes LIC in valuation
items.description: National Stock Exchange of India achieved a market capitalisation of ₹5 lakh crore for the first time recently. The stock closed at a record high of ₹2,070.05 on the BSE, up 4.02%. NSE surpassed Life Insurance Corporation of India in market value, now ranked as India's 10th most valued listed company. NSE shares gained significantly despite broader market movements, demonstrating strong investor interest.

items.title: Urban Company unveils QIP to raise Rs 2,500 crore
items.description: Urban Company has announced its intention to raise ₹2,500 crore through a qualified institutional placement. The company plans to invest ₹600 crore towards its InstaHelp business, focusing on rapid househelp services. Additionally, Urban Company will allocate funds for marketing initiatives and technology development. Some analysts remain cautious about the profitability of the instant help vertical. Urban Company's ongoing investments aim to solidify its market position amid competition.

items.title: BSE's BANKEX futures get CFTC nod to enter US market
items.description: In a significant development, the BSE has gained approval from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission for its BANKEX index futures contract, paving the way for American institutional investors to trade this innovative offering. The contract represents top banking stocks on the BSE, enhancing investment avenues in the banking sector.

items.title: Morgan Stanley expects Sensex to hit 95,000 in 2027
items.description: Morgan Stanley anticipates Indian equities will regain momentum by 2027, projecting the Sensex to rise significantly. The brokerage estimates the Sensex could reach 95,000 by December 2027, driven by several factors. Factors contributing to this rise include the improving earnings cycle and attractive valuations. Morgan Stanley favors domestic cyclicals and is overweight on consumer discretionary and industrials sectors.

items.title: D-Street extends winning streak on FPI inflows, easing crude prices
items.description: Indian equity indices saw gains supported by foreign fund inflows and stable crude prices on Monday. The BSE Sensex increased by 512.34 points, while the NSE Nifty rose by 146.80 points. Foreign Portfolio Investors were significant buyers, contributing ₹4,864 crore on the same day. However, domestic institutional investors sold equities worth ₹3,519 crore during the trading session. The broader market struggled, showing declines in midcap and smallcap indices.

items.title: Bank Nifty hits fresh record high, gains 14% since October 27
items.description: The Nifty Bank index achieved a new closing high of 61,575.90, reflecting a 0.9% increase. This surge was aided by the decline in crude oil prices and increased foreign investment in banking stocks. The index has seen a significant rally over the last three weeks, surpassing previous records. HDFC Bank led the gains with a notable increase, followed by other major banks.

items.title: Stocks in news: Adani Enterprises, BSE, Senco Gold, Hero Motors, HDFC Life, Anand Rathi Wealth and Urban Company
items.description: Indian equity markets witnessed a recovery on Monday, with modest gains recorded as the Nifty 50 index rose by 147 points, signaling renewed investor enthusiasm for large-cap stocks. In contrast, midcap and smallcap shares faced significant selling, creating a negative market breadth. Important announcements from Adani Enterprises and HDFC Life Insurance spurred interest among investors. A further upward trajectory may be possible after some minor price range consolidation.

items.title: D-St set for a cautious opening as GIFT Nifty signals muted start
items.description: Indian equity markets witnessed a modest rise, recovering some ground lost in recent sessions. Analysts noted a selective investor participation, indicating underlying market weakness. Heavyweight stocks contributed significantly to lifting benchmark indices, although caution is advised. Foreign portfolio investors made notable net purchases, while domestic institutions engaged in selling. The rupee gained against the US dollar due to foreign inflows and improving market conditions.

items.title: India's share of global m-cap hits 10-month high at 3.37%
items.description: India's global market capitalisation has seen a remarkable upswing since October, adding about $500 billion and reaching close to $5.42 trillion. This rebound has enabled India to reclaim its fifth-place ranking in the world. The return of foreign investors, after a substantial sell-off in AI stocks, is a testament to India's recovery against the backdrop of ongoing economic and market turbulence.

items.title: These large-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and an upside potential of over 25%
items.description: That market has seemingly shed the fear that was dominating it these past several months. However, even as a recovery takes place, it is not yet time to throw caution to the winds and make aggressive purchases. And that’s because there are still several unknowns in terms of geopolitics and the global markets.

items.title: Stock Radar: Falling fuel costs could lift IndiGo stock further; Shivangi Sarada recommends buying the stock
items.description: IndiGo's stock has shown signs of recovery after testing lower levels in October. Experts suggest buying the stock, anticipating a rise towards the 52-week high of Rs 5950. Strong upward momentum and supportive moving averages indicate a favorable trading environment. A key resistance level has emerged at Rs 5500 for traders to consider. Overall, the stock is reflecting positive trends influenced by falling crude oil prices.

items.title: As industry steps up activity, corporate borrowing follows
items.description: Corporate loan demand is increasing as companies in various sectors seek financing to support growth. The Reserve Bank of India's survey shows significant improvements in manufacturing capacity utilisation and order books. Public sector banks reported an increase in corporate lending pipelines, reflecting emerging investment trends. Investment is expanding across traditional and newer sectors, such as renewable energy and data centres.

items.title: NARCL gets 400 cr in resolution of Essel Group road co, beats estimate
items.description: NARCL has successfully resolved the account of Ludhiana Talwandi Toll Roads, exceeding the expected recovery amount. The joint venture includes Agrawal Infrabuild and Silica Infra, which will share equal stakes. The resolution plan was approved by the NCLT and completed in about 18 months, with the total recovery surpassing ₹400 crore. The toll road project faced operational delays and disruptions due to farmer protests.

items.title: Belrise Industries shares gain 10% in 2 days; Jefferies sees more upside. Time to buy now?
items.description: Belrise Industries has caught investors’ attention with a 10% rally in two sessions after posting 25% profit growth in Q2 FY27. Jefferies sees further upside, backed by the company’s expanding presence across automotive, aerospace and electronics manufacturing, and projects strong earnings growth through FY29.

items.title: Sebi may limit leveraged stock bets to curb volatility: Report
items.description: India's markets regulator is exploring potential limits on leveraged stock purchases amid increasing retail participation. Concerns have arisen as margin-funded stock bets have reached record levels in recent months. Discussions are ongoing regarding hard limits tied to a company's free float to manage risks effectively. While the regulator aims to mitigate market instability, it seeks to avoid disrupting retail investors' positions.

items.title: FIIs, MFs raise stakes in 5 largecap stocks for two straight quarters; shares rally up to 80%
items.description: Institutional investors, such as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and mutual funds (MFs), closely track companies through extensive research and analysis. Their shareholding patterns can offer valuable insights into institutional investment trends, particularly when both investor groups increase their exposure to the same stocks. An ET Markets analysis of shareholding data reveals that FIIs and mutual funds have raised their stakes for two consecutive quarters – April-June and July-September – in five large-cap stocks. Interestingly, all five stocks have delivered double-digit returns, with gains ranging from 12% to 80% in FY27 so far. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Laurus Labs shares rally over 5% as promoters rule out further stake sale
items.description: Laurus Labs shares rebounded after promoter Satyanarayana Chava ruled out further stake sales, easing concerns following a sharp sell-off. Reassurances on debt-funded personal transactions, ambitious capex plans and CDMO growth also supported investor sentiment.

items.title: Kaynes Technology shares down 16% in 2 days, but Jefferies still sees 22% upside. Should you buy?
items.description: Kaynes Technology shares have plunged over 16% in two sessions following a sharp Q2 earnings miss, prompting Jefferies to cut its price target to Rs 3,625 from Rs 4,480. The brokerage has retained its 'buy' rating, citing the company's expansion into semiconductor assembly and PCB manufacturing.

items.title: Why did market rise today? Sensex jumps 427 pts, Nifty closes above 25,350 for first time since Middle East war began. 4 factors explained
items.description: Although Diwali has come to an end, the stock market is witnessing a remarkable surge. The gains in Sensex and Nifty are primarily driven by falling oil prices and ongoing purchases by foreign investors. Furthermore, the rupee is strengthening thanks to these capital infusions and a favorable outlook on commodity prices. Banking stocks are leading the charge, fostering a positive sentiment in the market.

items.title: FirstCry shares rally 13% to one-month high. Why JM Financial sees 55% upside even after cutting target price
items.description: FirstCry operator Brainbees Solutions surged 13% after reporting improved Q2 FY27 results, with revenue rising 14% and net loss narrowing 75%. JM Financial retained its Buy rating but cut its target price to ₹245, citing expectations of sharp margin recovery and stronger growth from Q3 onwards.

items.title: Stock market investors vs economists: Nirmala Sitharaman gets contrasting capital gains tax recommendations for Budget 2027
items.description: Economists have urged Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to retain the 12.5% equity LTCG tax, countering demands from industry and foreign investors for relief. With FPI outflows mounting, the Budget 2027 decision could have significant implications for markets.

items.title: IT stocks gain from global AI worries, but Jefferies feels the sector is not out of the woods yet. Should you buy or avoid?
items.description: Jefferies cautioned that Indian IT stocks may face limited re-rating potential despite their recent recovery, citing subdued deal bookings, uncertain demand and rising subcontracting costs. While AI-related revenues and hiring improved in Q2 FY27, margin pressures and pricing competition persist. Coforge and Sagility remain its preferred sector picks.

items.title: FIIs are back with a record $11 billion. Jefferies names 10 largecap stocks to watch
items.description: Foreign portfolio investors have poured $11.4 billion into Indian equities since mid-October, marking a sharp reversal after two years of outflows. According to Jefferies, largecaps are emerging as the biggest beneficiaries, with the brokerage seeing further room for gains. FPI ownership in BSE 500 companies stood at a 12-year low of 17.3% in September.

items.title: Nifty Bank hits new record high as old warhorse HDFC Bank powers 13% November rally
items.description: The Nifty Bank index hit a fresh record high, rising 13% in November as HDFC Bank shares surged 17%. Strong credit and deposit growth have supported banking sector fundamentals, but analysts caution that the sharp rally has left the index overbought. They identify key support and resistance levels for traders.

items.title: Tata Sons IPO soon? Tata Chemicals, Tata Investment Corp shares rally up to 9% after RBI nudge to comply with listing norms
items.description: Tata Chemicals and Tata Investment Corporation shares rallied on Tuesday after the RBI reiterated that Tata Sons must comply with listing requirements for upper-layer NBFCs. The central bank's letter has renewed speculation around the holding company's long-awaited IPO, with several listed Tata Group companies holding stakes in Tata Sons.

items.title: Sensex rallies 600 points, Nifty above 25,400 as FII buying continues, oil prices ease. What lies ahead?
items.description: The Indian stock market experienced a substantial upswing, with the Sensex climbing 300 points to reach 82,402, and Nifty advancing almost 100 points above 25,350, driven by strong foreign institutional investor activity. Broader indices such as Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 250 also performed well. However, stocks like Tech Mahindra and Power Grid suffered slight declines of around 1%.

items.title: RBI may hike repo rate by 25-50 bps in December as inflation breaches 6%: Experts
items.description: India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, exceeding the Reserve Bank of India's upper limit. Experts anticipate that the RBI may hike the repo rate by 25 to 50 basis points in December. Persistent food inflation has raised concerns over price stability and household purchasing power. Market analysts suggest that a rate hike could influence borrowing costs and economic growth.

items.title: Traders pour cash into BlackRock’s India ETF as AI rout deepens
items.description: Investors poured over $316 million into BlackRock’s iShares MSCI India ETF last week, its largest weekly inflow since June 2025, as AI-related volatility drove diversification away from technology-heavy markets. Strong Indian equities, lower oil prices and improving earnings boosted sentiment, while foreign investors increasingly reversed their bearish positioning.

items.title: Blue Star among 4 stocks closing above VWAP
items.description: On November 17, the closing prices of four stocks in the Nifty500 pack were more than 1.5% above their respective VWAPs (Volume Weighted Average Prices), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data.VWAP represents the average price at which a stock traded during the day, with greater weight assigned to prices at which higher volumes were recorded. A closing price above VWAP indicates that the stock ended the session higher than its volume-weighted average traded price.
